resources.instruction: Frame of 01-brainstorm.md. ## Current state (the relevant part of the system, quoting file:line you read). ## Root problem and who is affected (restated in your own words). ## Assumptions: one line per assumption with code A-n and the state of evidence (checked / not checked) and HOW to check it. ## Options: 2-4 options, each under a ### heading with code P-n (if the system already has something usable, one option is "use what exists"), with description, pros, cons, risks, effort S/M/L, parts of the system affected. ## Recommendation: the chosen option, the reason, and why the others were rejected. ## Concrete requirements (output, scope, constraints). ## Open questions (each says who can answer and what changes if the answer is different). Keep the names and order of the ## headings; unused section: keep its heading, write "Not applicable: <reason>" (never delete it). The frame prescribes sections, not length: do not write to fill boxes, every sentence must carry decision information or evidence (file:line you read).

Frame of 02-spec.md. ## Goal. ## In scope. ## Out of scope (left out on purpose, with the reason). ## User stories. ## Business rules: code BR-n, one rule per line. ## Acceptance criteria: each AC is an item with code AC-n written as Given (when there is a precondition) / When / Then, verifiable by a test; it must cover the main path, error paths (missing input, wrong type, broken JSON), boundary values (length, empty, duplicate), and concurrent situations if there are parallel writes/deletes. ## Data and constraints. ## Known limitations (what is left undone on purpose and the remaining risks). ## Decisions made: code Q-n; a decision you chose yourself is marked "(self-chosen)" for the reviewer to confirm. ## Revision history (only when revised after feedback). Keep the names and order of the ## headings; unused section: keep its heading, write "Not applicable: <reason>" (never delete it). Length is up to you; the frame only requires every section to be present. Avoid sentences that only repeat the heading: each AC and BR must be concrete enough that a test can be written from it.

Frame of 03-design.md. ## Changes by layer (migration, entity, service, API, UI, client; each layer names the files/classes to change). ## API contract with example request/response (if the contract does not change: "Not applicable: <reason>"). ## Decisions and trade-offs: code D-n; each decision states the choice, the REJECTED OPTION and the reason for rejecting it (for example cascading delete relying on database configuration or an explicit delete in the service: choose one and say so). ## Test plan: for each AC-n of the spec at least one test line (name or description, level unit/integration/UI) and what it proves, error paths included. ## Risks and rollback: code R-n, each risk with its mitigation; how to undo a change that is hard to reverse. ## Out of scope (left out on purpose; later steps must not add it by themselves). tasks.json: the acceptanceCriteria of each task cite only AC-n codes that exist in 02-spec.md. Keep the names and order of the ## headings; unused section: keep its heading, write "Not applicable: <reason>" (never delete it). The frame does not ask for a longer document, only for all sections. Every decision must rest on code you read (cite file:line), not on guesses.
